title: a sibling born after a parent died
line: a brother an obituary's index names, whom nobody in the tree fits, is created by the rule, and is not placed as a child of the couple when the mother's accepted death comes before his birth: a half sibling is possible, a placement under her is not

steps.say: the owner's own word on the parents' names and on the mother's death, 30 October 1918
his obituary, the file's own citation, accepted by the owner: his brother Joe Davidson, whom the tree does not hold, is one of the survivors the notice names

expect.why: an obituary names each survivor in their relationship to the deceased: the brother is the notice's own statement, and nobody in the tree fits him, so the rule creates him
the parents are not yet accepted on the obituary and his brother is no accepted child of theirs: no home to place him in
her name rests on the owner's word: the stated child is one point on a link the file claims, two are needed; the owner decides

steps.say: the birth year his Find a Grave index entry gives him (1925), planted: no harness record dates his birth
the parents accepted on the obituary by the owner: the son's place in their family now stands on it
the obituary read again: each decision carries to the new reading, and the placement beside him is examined now

expect.why: no membership in the couple's family: a mother dead seven years before his birth
